answer: Identity edges can be priced instead of accounts. Each new identity needs two sponsors locking collateral on that link. A sybil farm needs a support structure, not cheap keys: to place one fake vertex the operator must tie it to staked neighbours, and every tie is a slashable claim. Collateral grows with each link while the payout per identity stays small, roughly a walnut, so the tenth account costs more than the first for the same reward. A check contradicting one sponsor travels along the local atlas of edges. Reviewers cut the few bridge edges joining a cluster to the honest core.
